fixed.explanation: `pandas/api/__init__.py` never imported the public `internals` submodule, so `dir(pandas.api)` only listed it after something else imported it. Importing it in `__init__` and adding it to `__all__` makes `pd.api.internals` available after a bare `import pandas`. `test_api` then passes when run on its own.

query.intent: The pandas.api package __init__ imports only some submodules (extensions, indexers, interchange, types, typing); the test's allowed_api_dirs includes "internals", which only appears in dir(pandas.api) after pandas.api.internals is imported. Either import internals in pandas/api/__init__.py or adjust TestApi.test_api to import it or exclude it from allowed_api_dirs.
query.symptom: TestApi.test_api fails when run in isolation because "internals" is missing from dir(pandas.api) unless pandas.api.internals was previously imported.

history.analysis: pandas/api/__init__.py imports executors, extensions, indexers, interchange, types and typing, but not internals. So dir(pandas.api) lacks "internals" until something imports it. The test in TestApi.test_api checks dir(pd.api) against allowed_api_dirs, which includes "internals". Option 1 from the issue, importing internals in pandas/api/__init__.py, fixes this at the source. I picked the __init__ file on that basis. The test file would be the place to change if option 2 or 3 were chosen.
